paragraphs: Car chargers are useful, but the problem with them is that you always need to find a cable. ESR’s Xtend 100W Retractable Car Charger solves that problem with two built-in USB-C cables that reel back in when you’re done.
With up to 100W of output and an extra USB-A port, it’s the car charger your vehicle is missing.

Car chargers are typically on the smaller side. The ESR Xtend takes up more room than most. Its bulky head will jut out of your car’s power socket further than a basic car charger will. However, the head can tilt up or down, so you can set it at an angle that works with your vehicle’s dashboard. That adjustable head makes a big difference. I can angle it so it’s easy to reach and doesn’t interfere with anything around the power socket.
The Xtend’s build quality is also decent. While the charger is made of plastic, it feels sturdy, with the matte sides giving it a premium in-hand feel.

The ESR Xtend car charger features two retractable nylon-braided USB-C cables. Each one extends to just over 3 feet (95 cm). That’s more than long enough for a front-seat passenger to use a phone while it’s plugged in. And since the cables retract independently, I can pull out one for my iPhone and leave the other tucked away until someone needs it.
ESR rates the Xtend for up to 100W of total output, with up to 67W from a single USB-C cable. Even with both cables in use, one can still deliver up to 67W while the other supplies up to 33W.

At 67W, there’s plenty of power to fast-charge an iPhone, an iPad or a compatible MacBook Air. The Xtend supports USB Power Delivery 3.2 with AVS, as well as PPS. That means it can fast-charge the iPhone 18 Pro and the latest Android devices.

Plugging in a third device drops the Xtend’s maximum output from 100W to 91W. ESR says the first USB-C cable can still deliver up to 67W, while the second USB-C cable and the USB-A port share the remaining 24W.
